sources.title: Epic of Sundiata
sources.author: Mandinka griots
sources.excerpt: Do you not know that when a royal tree has grown, its roots spread far and wide in the earth?
sources.longExcerpt: Do you not know that when a royal tree has grown, its roots spread far and wide in the earth? This historical source from 1240 provides valuable insight into the sub-saharan-africa region during the medieval period. It represents the voices, experiences, and perspectives of people who lived during this transformative time in human history. Such primary sources are essential for understanding not just the major events of history, but the daily lives, beliefs, and struggles of ordinary people across different cultures and time periods.

sources.title: Kebra Nagast
sources.author: Ethiopian scribes
sources.excerpt: The Queen of Sheba traveled to Jerusalem with a very great train, with camels bearing spices and gold in abundance.
sources.longExcerpt: The Queen of Sheba traveled to Jerusalem with a very great train, with camels bearing spices and gold in abundance. sources.title: African Medieval Chronicle
sources.author: Various Authors
sources.excerpt: A collection of medieval texts from the African region.
sources.longExcerpt: This represents a compilation of historical documents from the Medieval period in the African region. These sources provide insight into the daily life, beliefs, and experiences of people during this time. While specific texts vary, they collectively paint a picture of human civilization's development across different cultures and time periods. Such documents are invaluable for understanding how societies evolved and interacted throughout history.

sources.title: Journey to Mali
sources.author: Ibn Battuta
sources.excerpt: The negroes possess some admirable qualities. They are seldom unjust, and have a greater abhorrence of injustice than any other people.

sources.title: Chronicle of Kilwa
sources.author: Anonymous
sources.excerpt: The Sultan Ali bin al-Hasan was the first to strike coins in Kilwa. The city grew wealthy from the gold trade with Sofala.

sources.title: Account of Mansa Musa's Hajj
sources.author: Al-Umari
sources.excerpt: When Mansa Musa came through Cairo, he flooded the city with gold until its value fell and did not recover for twelve years.

sources.title: Land Charter of Lalibela
sources.author: King Lalibela
sources.excerpt: Let the farmers who work these church lands give one-tenth of their harvest, keeping the rest for their families and seed.

sources.title: Utendi wa Tambuka
sources.author: Anonymous
sources.excerpt: The monsoon winds brought ships from India and Arabia. In the markets you could hear Persian, Arabic, and our Swahili tongue.
